title: Template safe defaults policy (timeouts/retries/limits/cost caps) + guidance on how to communicate them
creator: Nikhil Sharma
related_links: Linear: PM-912 quickstart templates KPI and telemetry requirements
Linear: PM-913 define supported models for templates v1
GitHub: redwood-quickstarts PRs 101-115 (defaults + instrumentation + README standardization)
description:
Align on V1 safe defaults for Quickstart Templates (RAG + agents) and ensure they are (a) consistent across Python/TS, (b) configurable via env vars, (c) explained clearly in README/docs/code comments, and (d) don’t create surprise cost/latency or security footguns for self-serve users.

This ticket is the PM-level policy sign-off + comms plan: what we ship as defaults, what users can/should override, and what we must say explicitly (incl. “why” rationale).
acceptance_criteria:
- Canonical policy documented and reviewed (DevEx + SRE + Security) with explicit V1 default values.
- Each template README has a consistent “Safe defaults” section (table) and “How to tune” section (env vars + rationale).
- Code comments in template config modules reference the policy and call out cost/risk implications (e.g., max tokens, concurrency).
- Docs-site pages link to the policy and avoid conflicting default values.
- Support enablement: troubleshooting guidance references the same defaults (esp. 429s/timeouts/streaming disconnects).
- Any defaults that materially affect cost/quotas are conservative for self-serve (no surprise concurrency spikes).
decision_log:
Decisions (V1):
1) Timeouts are mandatory and explicit across LLM calls, retrieval, and tools.
   - API connect timeout: 3s
   - API overall non-streaming request timeout: 60s
   - Streaming idle timeout: 15s
   - Streaming max wall clock: 120s
   - Retrieval timeout: 10s
   - Tool call timeout: 15s
   Rationale: common failure modes are “hung” requests and proxies stalling streams; explicit timeouts reduce tail latency and improve debuggability.

2) Retries are idempotency-aware with exponential backoff + jitter.
   - max attempts: 3 total (initial + 2 retries)
   - base delay: 250ms; max delay: 5s; full jitter
   - retryable: 408/429/5xx + network errors; honor Retry-After on 429 (max sleep bounded)
   - non-retryable: 401/403/400/422/404 and validation failures
   Rationale: early template testers were amplifying rate limits via naive retry loops; bounded retries + honoring Retry-After is required.

3) Circuit breaker is required for outbound LLM calls.
   - open after 5 consecutive failures; open duration 30s; half-open trial requests 1
   Rationale: protects both Redwood and customers from thundering herd behavior and runaway costs during incidents.

4) Cost controls and bounded context.
   - max_output_tokens default: 512
   - soft max_input_tokens default: 8,000 (template reduces context via truncation/summarization strategy)
   - max_context_docs: 6
   - max_tool_output_chars: 20,000
   - agent_max_iterations: 6
   Rationale: avoid unbounded token growth in RAG/agent loops; keep defaults safe for self-serve quotas while still demonstrating value.

5) Client-side concurrency caps are required.
   - max concurrent in-flight LLM requests: 4
   - max concurrent tool calls: 4
   - recommended queue timeout: 2s
   Rationale: multiple reports of default concurrency patterns triggering 429s and confusing onboarding; default must be conservative.

6) PII-safe logging/tracing by default.
   - no raw prompts, retrieved docs, model output in logs or spans
   - debug logging must be opt-in and still redact common secret patterns
   - logs include correlation IDs + stable error codes
   Rationale: templates are copied into production; safe-by-default prevents accidental data leakage and reduces security review friction.

Communication decisions:
- There is one canonical “safe defaults and guardrails” source (Confluence) which templates and docs link to.
- READMEs show (a) the defaults table, (b) how to override via env vars, (c) “what happens when the guardrail triggers” (truncation, circuit open, tool validation fail).
- Code comments in config modules must include a one-line rationale per default (cost, reliability, safety) to reduce “why is this so low/high?” confusion.
implementation_notes:
Notes for DevEx/docs implementation (policy-to-product translation):
- README structure: follow the standardized template sections from DES-377. Add a consistent “Safe defaults” table near setup, not buried at the end.
- Env var naming: use REDWOOD_* schema (no language-specific drift). If a language needs an alias, keep it documented but treat REDWOOD_* as canonical.
- Avoid “magic” behavior: if truncation occurs, log a structured event + emit metric. Same for retries and circuit breaker open state.
- Avoid content leakage in examples: sample prompts and sample documents must be synthetic; logs/screenshots in docs must not contain real-looking PII.
- Streaming: templates should surface partial outputs on disconnect and be explicit about whether reconnect is attempted; do not silently replay tool actions.

Non-goals clarified:
- This ticket does not define customer-specific compliance posture; it defines baseline defaults suitable for broad use.
- This ticket does not attempt to maximize benchmark performance; it prioritizes predictable cost + reliability for onboarding.
